This is where short methodological notes live — the kind of thing that is
useful to write down but not worth a paper.

## Adding a post

Create a folder under `blog/posts/` with an `index.qmd` inside, e.g.
`blog/posts/2026-10-01-shrinkage-priors/index.qmd`. Give it a YAML header
with at least `title`, `description`, and `date`; the listing page picks it
up automatically. Keep images and data next to the `index.qmd` in the same
folder.

Plain Markdown works, so `index.md` is fine too if there is no code to run.

## Code

Posts can execute R or Python. A chunk looks like this:

````markdown

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 200)
plot(x, sin(x), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "steelblue", bty = "n")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A figure rendered at build time.](index_files/figure-html/fig-example-1.png){#fig-example width=672}
:::
:::

````

Cross-references (`@fig-example`), inline results, and citations from a
`.bib` file via `bibliography:` in the header all work as usual.

One thing to know: `freeze: auto` is set in `_quarto.yml`, so computed
output is cached in `_freeze/` and committed to the repo. Render **locally**
after changing code (`quarto render`), commit the `_freeze/` changes, then
push — GitHub then rebuilds the site without needing R or Python installed,
and without your package versions. Markdown-only posts need no local render
at all.
